concepts.name: MGNREGA: Legal Framework and Demand-Driven Architecture
key_dimensions: MGNREGA as a legal entitlement (not a scheme) under the MGNREGA Act 2005 — distinction from other welfare programmes
Demand-driven vs supply-driven employment: the 'right to work' principle and its enforceability
Role of Gram Sabha in identifying works vs. role of implementing agency — who has primacy
UPSC trap: MGNREGA guarantees employment to 'rural households' not 'individuals' — unit of entitlement

concepts.name: 100-Day Guarantee: Scope, Exceptions and Extensions
key_dimensions: Guarantee of 100 days per household per financial year — not calendar year
Conditions under which additional days can be provided (50 extra days for SC/ST households, drought/natural calamity extensions)
UPSC trap: The 100-day guarantee is to the 'household' — individual members within the household do NOT have separate entitlements
Comparison with Ayyankali Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme (Kerala) — urban vs rural scope of MGNREGA

concepts.name: Wage Payment Mechanism: Timelines, Delays and Compensation
key_dimensions: Mandatory wage payment within 15 days of work completion — else compensation at 0.05% per day delay
Wages paid directly to bank/post office accounts — role of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in plugging leakages
UPSC trap: MGNREGA wages are notified separately by the Centre for each state — NOT linked to state minimum wage (though must be at least equal post-2009 amendment)
Wage-material ratio mandate: at least 60:40 — implications for nature of permissible works

concepts.name: Permissible Works Under MGNREGA: Categories and Priorities
key_dimensions: Eight broad categories of permissible works (water conservation, land development, rural connectivity, etc.) — Schedule I of the Act
Priority order: individual beneficiary works for SC/ST/BPL/women-headed households vs community assets
Convergence with other schemes: PMGSY, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, watershed programmes
UPSC trap: Construction of buildings for gram panchayats is NOW permitted (2018 amendment) — earlier it was not

concepts.name: Unemployment Allowance: Trigger Conditions and Fiscal Responsibility
key_dimensions: Unemployment allowance payable when government fails to provide work within 15 days of demand
Rate: at least 1/4th of wage for first 30 days, at least 1/2 of wage thereafter
UPSC trap: Unemployment allowance is paid by the STATE government, NOT the Central government — fiscal incentive for states to provide work
Practical non-implementation of unemployment allowance — gap between legal provision and ground reality

concepts.name: Funding Pattern: Centre-State Cost Sharing
key_dimensions: Centre bears: 100% of unskilled wage cost, 75% of material and skilled/semi-skilled wage cost, administrative expenses
State bears: 25% of material cost, entire unemployment allowance, administrative costs of state council
UPSC trap: Unlike most Centrally Sponsored Schemes, the Centre bears ALL unskilled wage costs — not a standard 60:40 or 90:10 pattern
Implications of this funding pattern on states' incentive to provide employment vs allow unemployment allowance liability

concepts.name: Social Audit: Institutional Mechanism and Challenges
key_dimensions: Mandatory social audit of all works every six months by Gram Sabha — Section 17 of MGNREGA
Role of Social Audit Units (SAUs) — independent from implementing agency, facilitated by state but should be autonomous
UPSC trap: Social audit is a RIGHT of the Gram Sabha — workers can demand muster rolls, bills, vouchers as legally enforceable transparency
Challenges: capture of SAUs by local elites, low awareness, non-action on audit findings — MoRD's 2016 guidelines on follow-up action

concepts.name: Role of Gram Panchayat vs Line Departments: Implementation Hierarchy
key_dimensions: At least 50% of works must be implemented by Gram Panchayats (not contractors or line departments)
UPSC trap: MGNREGA explicitly BANS contractors and use of labour-displacing machinery — exceptions only for specific technical works
Programme Officer (Block level) and District Programme Coordinator — their powers and accountability
Conflict between GP autonomy and technical competence of line departments — governance tension

concepts.name: MGNREGA and Women's Participation: Mandates and Outcomes
key_dimensions: Statutory provision: at least 1/3rd of beneficiaries must be women — UPSC trap: this is a MINIMUM floor, not a cap
Actual female participation has consistently exceeded 50% nationally — significance for women's economic empowerment
Creche facility mandate for worksites with more than 5 children below age 6 — often overlooked provision
Feminist critique: MGNREGA reinforces gender wage gap if women are confined to lower-productivity MGNREGA work

concepts.name: MIS, e-Governance and Technology Integration in MGNREGA
key_dimensions: NREGASoft/MIS: real-time online tracking of job cards, muster rolls, fund flow — world's largest real-time public works MIS
Aadhaar-Based Payment System (ABPS): mandatory seeding — controversy over exclusion of genuine workers due to Aadhaar mismatches
UPSC trap: Supreme Court in Puttaswamy judgment held Aadhaar cannot be made mandatory for welfare schemes — tension with ABPS mandate
Geo-tagging of assets: before, during, after photographs — tool for asset quality verification and fund accountability

concepts.name: MGNREGA as Automatic Stabilizer: Counter-Cyclical Demand Management
key_dimensions: Surge in MGNREGA demand during COVID-19 (2020-21): expenditure reached ₹1.11 lakh crore — highest ever
MGNREGA as rural distress barometer: spikes in demand signal agrarian/economic stress
Keynesian argument for MGNREGA: multiplier effect of rural wage income on local consumption and non-farm economy
UPSC trap: MGNREGA is demand-driven — government cannot 'target' a specific number of households; expenditure is endogenous

concepts.name: Asset Creation Under MGNREGA: Quality, Durability and Convergence
key_dimensions: Categories of durable assets: water bodies, farm ponds, check dams, rural roads — impact on agricultural productivity
Criticism: assets created are often of poor quality, serve as 'make-work' schemes rather than productive investment
Convergence with PM Krishi Sinchai Yojana, PMGSY, SBM for complementary asset creation — 'convergence districts' model
UPSC trap: Individual beneficiary assets (land development, farm ponds) under MGNREGA require land ownership proof — excludes landless labourers

concepts.name: MGNREGA Wages vs Agricultural Wages: Distortion or Empowerment?
key_dimensions: Evidence that MGNREGA has raised rural wages by creating a floor — labour market tightening in agriculturally backward districts
Counter-argument: wage distortion reduces agricultural competitiveness and increases farmer costs — 'labour scarcity' problem
UPSC trap: MGNREGA wage rates are set by Centre via notification — states cannot set lower wages; but states CAN top up above central rate
Gender angle: MGNREGA's equal wage provision (same rate for men and women) — impact on narrowing rural gender wage gap

concepts.name: Gram Rozgar Sevak and Implementing Functionaries: Roles and Accountability
key_dimensions: Gram Rozgar Sevak (GRS): village-level functionary responsible for registering job card applications and maintaining records
Programme Officer at Block level: quasi-judicial powers to receive complaints — UPSC trap: PO must acknowledge work demand and is accountable for 15-day timeline
Ombudsman mechanism: independent ombudsman in each district for grievance redressal — rarely operationalized
Convergence with Panchayati Raj: MGNREGA strengthens GPs financially — GP receives 6% administrative charges for implementation

concepts.name: MGNREGA and Agricultural Productivity: Synergies and Trade-offs
key_dimensions: Farm ponds, check dams and irrigation channels created under MGNREGA — documented increase in irrigated area in BIMARU states
Kharif sowing season overlap: MGNREGA demand falls during sowing/harvesting — indicating workers prefer agricultural work when available
UPSC trap: MGNREGA permits work on private land ONLY for SC/ST, small/marginal farmers, IAY beneficiaries, differently-abled persons — not all farmers
MGNREGA + PM-KISAN convergence potential: addressing both income and employment dimensions of agrarian distress

concepts.name: Criticisms, Reforms and the 'Dole vs Development' Debate
key_dimensions: Economic Survey 2014-15 critique: MGNREGA as 'dole' — argument for replacing it with direct cash transfer (UBI debate)
Counter-argument by Drèze, Sen et al.: entitlement-based employment is superior to cash dole for dignity, asset creation and multiplier effects
Aruna Roy/Nikhil Dey critique from left: underfunding, delayed wages and contractor nexus hollow out the legal guarantee
UPSC trap: Government has consistently increased MGNREGA allocation in recent budgets despite periodic 'rationalization' rhetoric — actual vs stated policy

concepts.name: MGNREGA and Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes: Targeted Provisions
key_dimensions: SC/ST households entitled to 150 days (100 + 50 extra days) under drought/notification conditions — not automatic
Proportion of SC/ST beneficiaries as a performance metric — states with high SC/ST participation (Rajasthan, AP) vs laggards
UPSC trap: Extra 50 days are NOT automatically available to all SC/ST — they require state/Centre notification of distress or inclusion in a special category
Land development works on SC/ST patta land — convergence with land rights programmes like Forest Rights Act

concepts.name: Comparison with Global Public Works Programmes: Lessons and Positioning
key_dimensions: Comparison with Ethiopia's Productive Safety Net Programme (PSNP) — conditional vs unconditional, asset focus
South Africa's Expanded Public Works Programme — urban vs rural orientation vs MGNREGA's exclusive rural mandate
UPSC trap: MGNREGA is often cited as a model for 'Employer of Last Resort' (ELR) — but ELR in academic literature refers to government as full employment guarantor, not just 100 days
ILO recognition of MGNREGA as a global benchmark for social protection floors — soft power/diplomatic dimension

concepts.name: Fund Flow Mechanism and Pending Liabilities: Fiscal Stress
key_dimensions: Two-tier fund flow: Centre releases to state MGNREGA fund → district fund → GP — each tier has prescribed release timelines
Persistent pendency of wages and material dues — states run up arrears when Centre delays releases; workers bear the cost
UPSC trap: The MGNREGA Act does NOT specify a cap on total expenditure — government's budgetary allocation is a constraint, NOT a legal ceiling
CAG findings on MGNREGA fund diversion, inflated muster rolls and ghost workers — systemic fiduciary risks

concepts.name: MGNREGA's Impact on Poverty and Inequality: Evidence and Limitations
key_dimensions: Studies show MGNREGA reduces consumption poverty by 10-15% in high-intensity districts — IGIDR, World Bank findings
Impact on inequality: reduces rural-urban wage gap and within-rural inequality — Gini coefficient evidence
UPSC trap: MGNREGA addresses transient poverty (income smoothing) better than chronic poverty (structural deprivation) — distinction critical for poverty typology questions
Limitations: benefits concentrated in states with strong implementation (Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Kerala); Bihar, UP perform poorly — 'implementation gap' as binding constraint
